editorial:
Imagine being a kid with nobody in your corner, stuck in the dirty streets of old London. That is exactly where you find yourself with the main character in this gritty story. You follow a young orphan who is tired of being treated like a tool instead of a human being. The movie does a great job of showing you how scary and unfair the child labor market was back in the 18th century. It feels heavy at times, but the energy is high because you really want to see the kid fight back against the adults who are trying to keep him down. It is a rough ride, but it keeps you interested from the start.

The acting is what really sells it for you, especially the lead kid who makes you feel every bit of his anger. Some parts of the story move a bit slow, but the big emotional payoffs make it worth it. If you like stories about underdogs fighting the system, you will love this.
endingExplained: At the very end, you see the orphan lead a full-scale revolt of the other working children. They manage to burn down the factory where they were held captive, symbolizing their freedom. The big twist is that the man who seemed like a mentor was actually the one selling the kids. He gets caught in the fire, and the children escape to the docks to start a new life together as a found family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog stories and historical dramas.
similarMovies: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas
